name: AIRBNB
description: Airbnb JavaScript/TypeScript Style Guide - the most widely adopted JS/TS style guide.

rules.name: Use const/let
rules.description: Declare variables with const or let; var is not allowed.
rules.suggestion: Use const for constants and let for variables; var causes hoisting problems.

rules.name: Prefer const
rules.description: Use const whenever the variable is never reassigned.
rules.suggestion: Prefer const unless the binding needs to be reassigned.

rules.name: Single quotes
rules.suggestion: Use single quotes for strings, except where the string itself contains one.

rules.name: Template strings
rules.description: When building strings programmatically, use template literals instead of concatenation.
rules.suggestion: Use a template literal such as `${var}` instead of concatenation.

rules.name: Function expressions
rules.description: Prefer function expressions over function declarations.
rules.suggestion: Use a function expression or arrow function: const func = () => {}.

rules.name: Arrow functions
rules.suggestion: Use an arrow function for the callback so 'this' stays bound to the enclosing scope.

rules.name: Strict equality
rules.suggestion: Use === and !== to avoid the pitfalls of implicit type coercion.

rules.name: Braces in switch cases
rules.description: A switch case that declares a variable must be wrapped in braces.
rules.suggestion: Wrap the case body in braces {} to create a lexical scope.

rules.name: Naming - camelCase
rules.suggestion: Use camelCase for variables and functions, UPPER_CASE for constants and PascalCase for classes.

rules.name: Console usage
rules.suggestion: Remove console.log for production, or use a dedicated logging library.

rules.name: Semicolons
rules.description: Statements must be terminated with a semicolon.
rules.suggestion: Add semicolons explicitly to avoid problems caused by automatic semicolon insertion (ASI).
